To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dual use of technologies intensifies work-to-life conflict, especially for people who strive for a clear segmentation between work and private spheres.
the use of consumer IT for work purposes is related to WtLC, and that this effect is particularly strong for employees that strive to separate work and private life.
dual use of mobile IT is positively related to work-to-life conflict and that this relationship is stronger for people who desire a clear segmentation between work and life.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the implications of IT consumerization for employees’ work-to-life balance.
the dual use of technologies for both work- and private-life purposes.
the dual use of mobile IT and the resulting work-to-life conflict.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more employees are encouraged to use their own IT for work, the more they experience WtLC.
the dual-use of mobile IT is a driver of WtLC.
dual use is an important factor for WtLC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of private IT at work is a double-edged sword for employees.
the dual use of mobile IT and WtLC can only be managed if employees are given the opportunity to segment their work and private life.
the more employees are encouraged by their employer to use their own IT for both work and life, the more they are likely to experience WtLC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organizations should take the dual use of IT into account when developing policies regarding IT consumerization.
dual use of IT can be seen as a boundary-spanning behavior that intensifies WtLC.
the blurring of boundaries between work and life is not necessarily a good thing.
